text.p: The following are the main stories
from Monday morning's German newspapers:
FRANKFURTER ALLGEMEINE ZEITUNG

- The Free Democrats (FDP), junior partner in Chancellor Helmut Kohl's coalition government, go against the wishes of coalition partners by voting in favour of whole array of measures including a motion opposing tax hikes to help plug a budget hole at party congress at the weekend.
- Fire mostly destroys a Catholic church in the north German port of Luebeck and police launch arson investigation. Attackers scrawled swastikas on the church's brick facade.
- Bayern Munich clinch 14th German soccer championship with 4-2 win over VfB Stuttgart.
- Ministers in the former communist east Germany call on Federal government to set up and fund regional agencies to help with the running of privatised firms there.
HANDELSBLATT

- Ruling coalition strategists considering higher new borrowing after FDP categorically rules out higher taxes and postponing cuts to the solidarity tax -- levied to help fund German unification -- to plug budget gap.
- The early privatisation of Postbank to help relieve government budget could happen in the same way as last year's privatisation of remaining shares in Lufthansa.
- Oskar Lafontaine, leader of the opposition Social Democrats (SPD), says reduction in top tax rates is negotiable if tax hole filled some other way.
- German consumers are becoming more optimistic and are more ready to spend, according to the Icon consumer survey.
SUEDDEUTSCHE ZEITUNG
- FDP rejects filling budget holes wih tax rises. FDP party congress also wants to hold membership vote on party's stance towards conscription.
- Catholic church in Luebeck almost completely destroyed and police investigating possiblity of right-wing extremist arson after they found swastikas daubed on church walls.
- Bayern Munich are German soccer champions.
- SPD's Lafontaine no longer basically opposed to reduction of top rates of tax.
DIE WELT
- FDP party congress votes in favour of a hard line in dispute over taxation.
- Social committee of Kohl's Christian Democrats (CDU) rejects further cuts in social safety net.
- Luebeck church burnt down and attackers smear walls with swastikas.
